name: Wild Growth
oracle_text:
Enchant land
Whenever enchanted land is tapped for mana, its controller adds an additional {G}.
blocked_sentences: Whenever enchanted land is tapped for mana, its controller adds an additional {G}.

needs.what: Let the existing `add_mana_on_tap` static scope its `tapped_permanent` to the ONE permanent the source is attached to, rather than only to a class of permanent -- i.e. `{"tapped_permanent": {"attached": true}}`, the spelling every other Aura static already uses for "enchanted permanent". Concretely: `TAPPED_PERMANENT_KEYS` (src/automtg/cards/loader/vocabulary.py:66) gains `attached`; `_validate_add_mana_on_tap` (src/automtg/cards/loader/__init__.py:2053) accepts it beside the existing types/subtypes/supertypes and still requires `add_mana`; and `mana_added_on_tap` (src/automtg/engine/player_statics.py:258) checks the tapped `oid` against the static source's attached-to permanent before it runs the characteristic checks, so the two can be combined ("enchanted Forest"). The mana already goes to the player who tapped, which is exactly "its controller adds", so `affects_player: "any"` plus this key says the whole printed line. This one key unblocks the whole aura-ramp family that prints the same sentence -- Wild Growth, Utopia Sprawl, Fertile Ground, Overgrowth, Market Festival, Weirding Wood, Trace of Abundance. Utopia Sprawl needs one more thing on top of it (its added mana is a colour chosen as the Aura entered, which `add_mana` cannot read off the permanent); Wild Growth's fixed {G} needs nothing but this.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `add_mana_on_tap` is the right effect and is already in the right place: `mana_added_on_tap` (src/automtg/engine/player_statics.py:258) is consulted at the mana choke point from `costs.py:574`, so its mana joins the pool immediately without using the stack, which is what a triggered mana ability must do (605.1b / 605.4a). What it cannot say is WHICH permanent. `TAPPED_PERMANENT_KEYS` is frozen to `{types, subtypes, supertypes}` and is matched against the tapped permanent's current characteristics as a class, and `_validate_add_mana_on_tap` explicitly REFUSES `affects` on this effect ("takes 'affects_player', 'tapped_permanent', 'add_mana' and an optional 'condition', and no 'affects' or 'amount'") -- so `affects: {"attached": true}`, the exact spelling Alexi's Cloak and Arcane Flight use for "enchanted creature", is a load error here. `affects_player` is not a substitute: it narrows WHOSE taps count ("you" for Crypt Ghast, "any" for Vernal Bloom), never which permanent, and its reach is the whole battlefield. The only approximation available, `{"affects_player": "any", "tapped_permanent": {"types": ["Land"]}}`, is Vernal Bloom's card and not this one: in the sandbox it would make all 30 lands each add an additional {G} off a one-mana Aura enchanting exactly one of them. `static_condition_keys`' `is_attached` only asks whether the Aura is attached to something, not what was tapped. `double_land_mana` (Vorinclex) is the other tap-for-mana static and is wrong twice over -- every land its controller taps, and it copies a type that land produced instead of a fixed {G}. The triggered spelling is worse, not merely uglier: `{"event": "ability_activated", "mana_ability": true, "filter": {"attached": true}}` looks exact, but game.py:1209 documents that only the BY-HAND activation path emits it -- the mana abilities the payment solver taps to pay for a spell go through `costs.pay_mana` -> `activate_mana_ability` and emit nothing at all -- so the trigger would be silent in precisely the case the card is played for; and even when it did fire, a triggered ability queues and drains at the next priority (603.3), so the extra {G} would arrive after the spell had already been paid for. It also asks the wrong question (any activation of a mana ability, tapping or not). The `becomes-tapped` gap already on file is a third, separate event: a land becomes tapped by attacking or by an opponent's Icy Manipulator without being tapped for mana, and the solver's auto-tap fires no activation trigger at all, so neither event is the other's substitute. The rest of the card is expressible -- "Enchant land" is the card-level target `{"id": "enchanted", "kind": "permanent", "selector": {"types": ["Land"], "zone": "battlefield"}}` -- but with the only printed ability blocked there is nothing to write a partial answer around.
